source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Diarrhea shortly after weaning can kill pigs quickly and needs urgent attention — the most common cause is E. coli bacteria, especially within 3 weeks of weaning in pigs removed from the sow before 6 weeks old. Other causes include whipworm, nodule worm, swine dysentery, salmonellosis, and (in pigs older than 3–5 months) ileitis. Weaning pigs only once they reach 6–8kg (rather than by age alone), keeping the weaner housing warm, dry, and at a constant temperature, and providing clean water all reduce risk. If diarrhea occurs, provide electrolytes in drinking water and treat with antibiotics appropriate to age: apramycin or neomycin (or trimethoprim combinations, penicillin, oxytetracycline) for pigs under 12 weeks; lincomycin, tylosin, olaquindox, tiamulin, or tetracyclines for pigs over 12 weeks.
caveat: Medication names and dosages are reproduced from the source manual for reference only. Product availability, correct dosing, and withdrawal periods vary by country and should be confirmed with a local veterinarian or extension officer before use.
